name: The Armour household at 2115 Prairie Avenue
head: pa1904_armour_mrs_philip_d

present_on_scene_date.note: Listed at 2115 Prairie Avenue in the Blue Book for 1904 (canvass begun September 1903) and again in the 1905 edition (canvass begun September 1904), which bracket 1 July 1904. The 1905 list prints: 2115 Mrs. Philip D. Armour.

associated_with.note: The Blue Book's Prairie Avenue street list prints the household at 2115, and the 1905 list again. The book gives no date the household came or went, so neither end is dated here.

not_in_this_household.note: WHO IS NOT ON THIS CARD, AND WHY. The Blue Book is a society register: it names the family members who received and were received, prints unmarried daughters only as '& dr.', and names no young children, servants, coachmen, cooks or nurses. The 1900 census (ED 40, T623 roll 245) was read for this card. The seven live-in staff it lists at the house on 1 June 1900 are on the card, graded inferred because the count was taken four years before the scene. Left off: P. D. Armour (Philip D. Armour died in January 1901; the 1904 Blue Book lists his widow); Alice Shaw (a widow of 58 with the relation column left blank; no 1904 source puts her here); Kenneth Monroe (heads his own family in the rear building; his trade reads as a horseman but is hard to read). The 1910 census was not read. A person goes on this card when a source names them, and not before.

persons.name: Mrs. Philip D. Armour
persons.note: The meat-packer's widow; the Prairie Avenue marker says the house was 'for nearly 50 years the home' of the Armour family and that his widow died there in 1927. The 1900 census lists Belle O. Armour here as wife, born April 1843 (the figures are hard to read), in Ohio, married (ED 40, sheet 14B, line 69, leaf n821).

persons.name: Delia King

born.note: The census gives July 1874, age 25 on 1 June 1900.

occupation.note: Written as "Parlor maid" in the occupation column on 1 June 1900.

persons.note: Enumerated on 1 June 1900 in the house, as a servant (parlor maid); born July 1874, in Ireland, came to the United States in 1892, single. Servants changed places often, so this records who worked here in 1900; no source read says whether this person was still here on 1 July 1904. Part of the name is hard to read on the sheet; this is the best reading.
